newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Investor says Scania Q3 disappointing.
newsitem.headline: Investor says Scania Q3 disappointing.

text.p: Swedish industrial investment company Investor AB, which has strategic holdings in many of the country's leading blue chip companies, said on Monday the third quarter performance of Scania AB was disappointing.

In April, Investor completed the sale of a 55 percent stake in truck and bus maker Scania which is now classed among its main holdings alongside drug-maker Astra, technology group Incentive, forestry concern Stora and others.

Investor said the market value of its main holdings had risen to 53.12 billion crowns ($8.02 billion) at end-September from 49.28 billion at the end of 1995, but figures showed the increase would have been greater if Scania were excluded.
Divesting a large stake in Scania at a good price had given Investor a 12.4 billion crown capital gain.
"And we now have strong cash reserves for new investments," managing director Claes Dahlback said in a statement.
"When it comes to Scandia, regrettably we must say the results for the third quarter did not come up to expectations.

"No one could have foreseen at the time of Scania's (separate) listing that costs for production switchover to the new models, as well as the negative effects of currency fluctuation would have been that high."

Investor said its net worth, considered the most appropriate figure on which to judge an investment company, rose to 73.2 billion crowns by September 30 compared with 51.23 billion at the end of last year.
This equated to 366 crowns per share compared with 257 crowns.
Net worth grew further to 74.11 billion crowns as of November 13 this year, Investor said in its nine-month report.

Scania, now a stand-alone company which is no longer consolidated in Investor, reported on November 7 a sharp fall in profit after financial items of 2.14 billion crowns versus 3.51 billion a year earlier.

Saab AB, which embraces Saab's aerospace and defence companies but not Saab Automobile, is still wholly owned by Investor. It reported a fall in profit after financial income and expenses to 84 million crowns from 223 million at the same time last year.
Saab Automobile, jointly owned by Investor and America's General Motors Corp, did not report nine-month figures.
